answer: Rooted reputation decay: each new identity starts on a low knoll, earning trust only through sustained interaction. Reputation erodes when inactive, like a vine losing grip, so disposable identities must keep paying upkeep or fade. Identity creation also requires proof of accumulated outgoing work—paid in compute or escrow—that scales with the square of recently created identities, a karst of rising cost. Cloning costs compounding upfront work plus continuous upkeep per identity, so mass sybils face superlinear expense.
